all be fully completed within one TSG cycle/quarter in all affected WGs. C. TEI Work Item codes shall not be used where another appropriate Work Item code exists. D. Inter-TSG aspect: D1. Normally, for TSG SA/CT work that requires cat.B/C CRs from RAN WGs a RAN WI is required. D2. In case the RAN work triggered via a TSG SA/CT WI* is small and it affects only one RAN WG, then the RAN WG CR(s) shall use the WI code* of the TSG SA/CT WI that triggered this work. *NOTE: provisional WI codes, companion WIDs/"mini-WIDs" are not meant here but already TSG approved proper WIs. D3. It is not possible to trigger work in RAN WGs via TEI CRs coming from TSG SA/CT or SA/CT WGs. The same applies for the reverse direction. Cases identified by the RAN WGs have to be reported to TSG RAN and the affected TSG (SA or CT) stating that an SA/CT WI is required for RAN to undertake the work. E. Inter-RAN WG aspects: E.1 It is mandatory to fill out the "other specs affected" field for all CRs, i.e. either Yes or No shall be ticked and if Yes is ticked all TSs/TRs impacted by each CR shall be indicated, referring to the exact CR numbers to those TSs/TRs and this for the present WG and all other WGs that have CRs linked to the present CR. TEI CRs missing this information or having wrong information shall not be approved. Exception: for test specifications mentioned in the "other specs affected" field, it is not required to mention CR numbers. E.2 Each TEI cat.B/C CR and each TEI cat.F/A CR that corrects functionality related to an earlier TEI cat.B/C CR shall have a unique TEI identifier in square brackets [ ] at the end of the CR title on the CR cover sheet. TEI cat.B/C CRs and follow-up TEI cat.F/A CRs without such a unique TEI identifier cannot be approved at RAN. The usage of [ ] in CR titles for other purposes than TEI identifiers shall be avoided as they may be interpreted as TE

TEI cat.B/C CRs and follow-up TEI cat.F/A CRs without such a unique TEI identifier cannot be approved at RAN. The usage of [ ] in CR titles for other purposes than TEI identifiers shall be avoided as they may be interpreted as TEI identifiers. TEI identifiers are strings (max. 18 characters or less) composed of letters (upper and/or lower case), digits (0..9) and underscores (_). The usage of hyphens should be avoided. No blanks or special characters (like e.g. :;.,!?<>"£%^&*(){}+=@#~'/\|) shall be used in TEI identifiers. A TEI identifier is case sensitive (i.e. [ABCDE] and [abcde] are different TEI identifiers). However different TEI identifiers that differ only by case shall not be used. Follow-up TEI cat.F/A CRs require the same unique TEI identifier as the original cat.B/C CRs. If TEI crosses WG boundaries, all impacted WGs have to use the same unique TEI identifier. E.3 WG chairs reports report to TSG RAN about all agreed and technically endorsed cat.B/C TEI CRs and all
